newsitem.title: INDIA: Gold - Indian sub-continent demand seen mixed.
newsitem.headline: Gold - Indian sub-continent demand seen mixed.

text.p: Demand for gold in India was reviving as the second wedding season got underway and domestic political uncertainty fuelled safe-haven buying, but the market remained dull in neighbouring Pakistan, dealers said on Monday.
They said an on-going shopping festival in Dubai, the feeder market for gold demand in the Indian sub-continent, had yet to gather tempo.
Babubhai Jain, a leading jeweller, said a second round of India's marriage season began this month and will last for two months. The first, lasting four months, ended in February.
Dealers said India's latest bout of political uncertainty could further fuel demand for gold.
India's 13-party United Front (UF) coalition government has been pushed to the brink of collapse with its main ally, the Congress Party, withdrawing support.
Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's government is due to face a vote of confidence in parliament on Friday.
"Political uncertainty in the country is expected to drive more investors to pull their money out of securities and put it in gold in the next few weeks," Jain said.
On the Bombay bullion market, standard gold gained 65 rupees to 4,780 rupees per 10 grammes in the week to Monday, on fresh seasonal buying, aided by limited supplies.
Jain said gold supplies had been limited following a drop in imports and suspension of the sale of confiscated gold by Bombay customs. Customs had sold about 200 kg of gold last month.

Dealers said imported gold did not leave much margin because of a premium of 13.50 percent that buyers pay to acquire a special licence to import the metal, in addition to a duty of 220 rupees per 10 grammes.
In Karachi, Pakistan's main commercial city, dealers expected gold prices to stay mixed in the current week due to lower demand for gold.
"The demand from jewellers is low and may keep the prices slightly depressed," one dealer said.
In the week to Monday, standard gold dropped 12 rupees to 4,694 rupees per 10 grammes.
Dealers in Dubai said the month-long shopping festival which began on March 27 had raised the appetite for retail gold.
"The festival is going well but it's slower than last year. There are too many campaigns going on. There are too many offers on the market. It's healthy but it's not booming," said one.
"You can get a good deal everywhere. They are giving away Rolls Royces, BMWs and lots of other things," he added.
Backers of the Dubai Shopping Festival (DSF) and its parallel "Dubai city of gold" promotion, have high hopes that the events will boost sales, with an expected two million visitors.
Tourists from the Indian-subcontinent and other Gulf Arab states are expected to empty their wallets in Dubai where taxes are lower than in other regional markets and close to spot market rates.
But an anticipated revival of wedding season demand for gold from mid-April would strengthen the market, traders said.
